faq.q: Straight or curved lame: which should I gift?
faq.a: A straight blade cuts clean, upright lines and decorative patterns. A curved blade sits at an angle and lifts a tall ear on a batard. If you don't know their style, a straight UFO is the safer first gift.

faq.q: Are replacement blades easy to find?

faq.q: Impact mill or stone mill: which should I gift?
faq.a: Impact mills like the Classic and Impact are fast and make fine bread flour. Stone mills like the Harvest and Flourish run slower and cooler and give a classic stone-ground texture. For bread, either works. Speed favors impact, character favors stone.

faq.q: Do I need a special mixer for whole grain dough?
faq.a: Whole grain dough is heavy. A bottom-drive mixer like the Bosch Universal Plus or Artiste handles it without the strain that tilt-head mixers feel.

faq.q: How does the ACADEMY26 code work?

faq.q: Which grain should a new home miller start with?
faq.a: Hard white wheat. It mills easily and bakes into a light, mild whole wheat loaf. Once they're comfortable, einkorn and spelt add flavor.

faq.q: Can I bake with einkorn like regular flour?
faq.a: Mostly. Einkorn absorbs less water and has weaker gluten, so use a little less liquid and expect a softer dough. The flavor is worth it.
